Evidence: Navjot Singh Sidhu, the Punjab Congress chief, stated that 'dissidence in Congress is less compared to rivals' amid discussions of factionalism within the party ahead of the Assembly polls. He emphasized the party's commitment to resolving disputes and respecting all leaders, indicating a belief in lower internal conflict relative to other parties. This assertion was made during a time when the Congress faced protests over candidate selections, but Sidhu maintained that the level of dissent was not as high as in rival parties (Source 1).
Justification: The retrieved evidence directly supports the claim made by Sidhu that dissidence in Congress is less compared to rivals. Source 1 explicitly quotes Sidhu asserting this point amidst discussions of factionalism, indicating that he believes internal conflicts are less severe than those in competing parties. Therefore, the evidence corroborates the core assertion of the claim.
